title: Patagonia vs Iceland: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Iceland for first-timers, variety, and ease of logistics. Patagonia for serious multi-day trekkers with 10+ days and solid fitness. Budget: Iceland $120–180/day all-in (self-drive); Patagonia $100–160/day on the ground plus expensive long-haul flights.

categories.name: Daily Budget
categories.summary: On the ground, Patagonia runs $100–160/day vs Iceland's $120–180/day. But total trip cost favors Iceland once you add cheaper flights and no park permit fees.

categories.name: Hiking Quality
categories.summary: W Trek and O Circuit in Torres del Paine are among the world's best multi-day treks. Iceland has excellent day hikes but can't match Patagonia's sustained backcountry trekking.

categories.name: Ease of Logistics
categories.summary: Iceland's Ring Road is self-driable with minimal advance planning. Patagonia requires permits booked 6+ months ahead and complex multi-leg transport.

categories.name: Northern Lights
categories.summary: Iceland delivers reliable Aurora Borealis viewing Sep–Mar. Patagonia's Southern Lights are rare and unpredictable.

categories.name: Wildlife
categories.summary: Iceland wins for puffins, whales, and foxes. Patagonia wins for condors, pumas, and penguin colonies.

categories.name: Unique Experiences
categories.summary: Iceland has 5–6 world-exclusive experiences (aurora, inside-a-volcano, snorkeling tectonic plates, midnight sun). Patagonia goes deep on 2–3 (glacier trekking, multi-day wilderness, penguins).

categories.name: Flight Access
categories.summary: Direct flights from Europe; $500–700 from USA East Coast. Patagonia requires 2–3 legs and runs $900–1,500 from North America.

categories.name: Towns & Infrastructure
categories.summary: Reykjavik is a genuinely great city. Puerto Natales is functional but basic — expensive for what it offers.

categories.name: Weather Predictability
categories.summary: Both are notoriously changeable. Patagonia has extreme wind gusts (120 km/h). Iceland has 'four seasons in a day.' Pack layers for both.

categories.name: Accessibility
categories.summary: Iceland's highlights are reachable with minimal hiking. Patagonia demands 5–8 days of loaded-pack trekking to see the best scenery.

faq.question: Is Patagonia or Iceland better for hiking?
faq.answer: Patagonia for serious multi-day trekking (W Trek, O Circuit). Iceland for accessible day hiking with variety.

faq.question: Which is cheaper, Patagonia or Iceland?
faq.answer: Similar on the ground, but Iceland is cheaper total trip cost due to lower flight prices. Campervans make Iceland very budget-friendly.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit?
faq.answer: Patagonia: November–March (austral summer). Iceland: June–August (midnight sun) or September–March (Northern Lights).
